title: Saving a file is not a Git commit
subtitle: Understand the working tree, staging area and commits.
concept: Saving changes the working tree. git add stages the content at that moment. git commit records staged content locally.
intuition: A draft on your desk, a version inside an envelope and a sent letter are distinct. Editing the draft does not change the envelope.
objectives: Use status to inspect branch and file states, then read relevant diffs.
Verify the change and create a focused local commit.

body.title: Know which repository you are in
body.text: Git records versions; GitHub can host repositories. In a new practice directory, git init -b main creates a repository. Use git clone for an existing remote project; do not casually initialize inside another repository. Start with git status. Repository-local user.name and user.email set commit identity here; a public commit can expose that email.

body.title: Three versions can differ
body.text: The working tree holds current files; the index stages the next commit; HEAD identifies the checked-out commit, usually the branch tip. After git add README.md, later edits do not update its staged version. git diff compares working tree with index; git diff --staged compares index with HEAD. New unstaged files normally need status and direct inspection too.

body.title: Give each commit one purpose
body.text: Read diffs, run relevant checks and stage explicit files before committing. Describe the reason, such as reject whitespace-only plans. .gitignore prevents ordinary addition of matching untracked files, including dependencies and local secrets. It neither removes tracked content nor erases leaked history.

formalDefinition.text: Saving changes the working tree. git add stages the content at that moment. git commit records staged content locally.
conditions: For small personal learning projects. In shared repositories, follow the team's conventions.
This method produces checkable evidence; it cannot guarantee arbitrary AI output is correct.

workflow: Use status to inspect branch and file states, then read relevant diffs.
Stage only intended files and inspect the staged diff.
Verify the change and create a focused local commit.

workedExamples.title: A first practice commit
workedExamples.problem: Record README in a new learning-list practice directory.
steps: Initialize main and configure this repository's identity.
Save README.md, inspect it and stage it.
Review the staged diff, commit and inspect the log.
workedExamples.answer: Use init only in a new practice repository; start existing projects with status. Create and save README.md first, and replace the identity placeholders with your chosen public commit identity.
workedExamples.code:
git init -b main
git config user.name "Your Name"
git config user.email "your-public-email@example.com"
git status
git add README.md
git diff --staged
git commit -m "Document how to run the study list"
git log --oneline

workedExamples.title: Editing after staging
workedExamples.problem: v1 is committed. Edit to v2 and stage it, then edit to v3. Without staging again, what is committed?
steps: HEAD is v1, index v2, working tree v3.
Ordinary diff shows v2 to v3.
Staged diff shows v1 to v2.
workedExamples.answer: The commit records v2. The working tree remains v3 with unstaged changes. To commit v3, review and stage it first; commit does not collect every latest edit automatically.

commonMistakes.correction: Editor saving only writes the working tree; staging and committing are separate.

commonMistakes.claim: git add . is always the best choice.
commonMistakes.correction: It may include unrelated files. Inspect status and prefer explicit paths while learning.

practice.problem: Working tree v3, index v2, HEAD v1: what happens on commit without add?
practice.answer: HEAD becomes v2; working tree stays v3 with its unstaged diff.
solution: Committing does not automatically overwrite your working edits.

practice.problem: Does empty ordinary diff mean nothing can be committed?
practice.answer: No. Changes may already be staged; inspect git diff --staged and status.
solution: Check status for new files too.

practice.problem: How do you stage only the instructions?
practice.answer: git add README.md, then git diff --staged to check for other content.
solution: Check the staged scope before committing.

practice.problem: If .env reached public history, does ignoring it fix the leak?
practice.answer: No. Revoke or rotate exposed credentials first, then follow repository procedures to remove tracking and clean history.
solution: Stop using the compromised secret first.
Ignore rules only prevent ordinary addition of matching untracked files.

learningCheck.question: After staging and then editing, what does commit record by default?
feedback: Commit does not run add again automatically.
The index supplies the next commit.
Local commits do not read a remote webpage.

feedback: Inspect branch and change states first.
Push does not explain local staging.

steps.question: With index v2 and working tree v3, what does ordinary diff compare?
feedback: Ordinary diff compares index and working tree.
Remote content is not the default comparison.
